title: Investigating Out-of-Distribution Generalization of GNNs: An Architecture Perspective

problem.claim: Graph neural networks may generalize poorly when test graphs come from a distribution different from the training distribution.

gap.claim: Existing graph OOD generalization work has mainly used data-driven and strategy-based approaches, with limited attention to the effects of GNN architectures.

contributions.claim: The work investigates graph OOD generalization through the common building blocks of modern GNN architectures.
The work provides theoretical insights and discussion intended to explain the observed effects of architectural components on graph OOD generalization.
The work develops DGat, a GNN backbone combining graph self-attention and a decoupled architecture.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that graph self-attention and decoupled architectures improve graph OOD generalization, while a linear classification layer tends to reduce it.
The authors report that DGat achieves substantial and consistent improvements under graph OOD across various training strategies.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNN performance commonly assumes matching training and test distributions, but real-world graph data may violate this assumption.
Graph OOD research has focused mainly on data-driven and strategy-based methods, leaving architectural effects comparatively understudied.
The work examines common GNN building blocks and reports different effects of self-attention, decoupled architectures, and linear classification layers.
The reported architectural insights motivate the DGat backbone, which combines the two positively associated properties.
The authors report consistent improvements for DGat across multiple training strategies under graph OOD conditions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports positive OOD effects for graph self-attention and decoupled architectures, but a negative tendency for a linear classification layer.

interpretation.claim: Architectural choices may materially influence OOD behavior independently of data or training-strategy changes.

application.claim: When improving graph OOD robustness, compare architectural components explicitly rather than evaluating only data or training strategies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that these architectural effects transfer to all graph tasks, datasets, or distribution shifts.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, tasks, or OOD shift definitions used.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or experimental settings.
The abstract does not state the exact theoretical assumptions or results.
The abstract does not describe DGat's detailed architecture or computational trade-offs.
